subject: Order form: payment routing, tax responsibility, and net30 + credit note flow
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acme-analytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: James Patel <james.patel@acme-analytics.com>, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on order form invoicing and taxes

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for sending the updated order form. We have a few finance items we need clarified before we can route to our AP team:

1) Invoice split: our legal wants the option to receive a single master invoice for the entire annual commit, rather than monthly invoices per product. Is Redwood able to issue a consolidated annual invoice (with monthly line items) and still support net30?

2) Tax responsibility: Acme will provide a tax exemption certificate for applicable jurisdictions. Can Redwood apply the exemption at invoice time, or do you require upfront documentation before you remove tax?

3) Credit notes / adjustments: If we overconsume one quarter and request a credit against the next quarter, what's the process and timeline? Any constraints around issuing credit notes for usage-based invoices?

We attached the filled purchase order and referenced the latest OrderForm_Acme_v3.pdf. Would appreciate a quick call this week if needed.

Thanks —
Olivia Barnes
Head of Procurement, Acme Analytics

Attachment: PurchaseOrder_ACME_4432.pdf (application/pdf, 92 KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on order form invoicing and taxes

Hi Olivia —

Quick answers inline, and copying our finance and sales lead to scope changes:

1) Consolidated invoice: We can support a consolidated annual invoice with monthly line item breakdowns for reporting, but our standard hosted billing system currently issues monthly invoices by default. To issue a single annual invoice we'd need a manual billing arrangement (one-time invoice) and a PO/commit to lock the amount. That typically requires a lead time of ~10 business days before the first charge period.

2) Tax exemption: We can accept a tax exemption certificate after signature and apply it prospectively to future invoices. For retrospective tax removal we'd need to reissue invoices and potentially process credits — finance will confirm constraints below.

3) Credit notes: We issue credit notes for usage disputes or agreed adjustments; standard SLA is 30 days to review and 14 days to apply the credit to the next invoice once approved. Credits for consumption-based overages are handled case-by-case and require approval from Finance.

Next steps: Ben, can you confirm if Acme is on a committed annual plan (minimum commit confirmed in Section 2 of the order form)? Marissa, can Finance confirm whether we can support the requested consolidated annual invoice and the retroactive tax application policy?

If it helps, happy to set a 30-minute sync.

Best,
Rachel
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: OrderForm_Acme_v3.pdf (application/pdf, 220 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on order form invoicing and taxes

Rachel —

Acme is a committed annual deal (they've signed for 1.5M USD annual commit per the SOW), so they're asking for two commercial accommodations: consolidated invoice and tax exemption handling.

From a seller perspective: consolidated invoice is ok for closed/wired deals but ops will want net30 preserved and a clear payment routing (wire instructions or AP email). Also need to ensure our revenue recognition / billing engine can accept a single invoice without breaking our monthly reporting — Marissa, flag if there are GAAP/RR concerns.

On tax: Acme says they will provide TaxCert_Acme.pdf. The ask to apply the exemption retroactively (remove tax from prior invoices) is sticky — we should avoid manual re-billing unless necessary. Lauren, can legal confirm whether we accept tax removal only prospectively and document this in the order form? If legal is comfortable with a limited retro credit (e.g., credits only for the last 90 days), we can offer that as a compromise.

Also, procurement asked about credit notes for usage adjustments — recommend stating a 45-day review window in the order form and that credits apply only to future invoices (no cash refunds except in exceptional cases).

I'll be on the sync if scheduled.

— Ben
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 12:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on order form invoicing and taxes

Ben / Rachel —

Legal read here. Summary of recommended redlines for the Order Form and MSA to address Acme's asks: 

• Consolidated invoice option: Add language to Section 4.2 (Invoicing) that "Customer may elect, at time of execution, to receive a consolidated annual invoice. Redwood will issue such invoice within 10 business days and apply the then‑current payment terms (Net 30). For accounting purposes, Redwood will include monthly line item detail for Customer reporting."

• Tax exemption: Add a clause to Section 5 (Taxes) stating "Customer shall provide valid tax exemption certificates. Redwood will apply exemptions prospectively. Retroactive tax removals will be considered only if Customer provides necessary documentation within 60 days of the original invoice date; any approved retroactive adjustments will be processed as credit notes applied to the next invoice."

• Credit notes and adjustments: Add a process in the SOW: disputes submitted within 45 days, Finance to review within 30 days, credits applied to next invoice. No cash refunds except for exceptional approvals by Finance+Legal.

• Invoice routing and payment instructions: Add a block to Appendix A for "Billing & Payment Details" capturing AP email, PO#, and wire instructions to avoid routing issues.

• Minimum commit / purchase order: Clarify that consolidated invoice does not alter the committed spend or revenue recognition; include language that manual invoicing requests may incur a one-time ops fee of $1,500 to cover special billing handling.

I'll prepare a redline document (Redlines_Redwood_Legal.docx) and a short companion email that sales can send to Acme. From a risk perspective, prospectively applying tax exemptions and limiting retroactive credits to 60 days is reasonable.

— Karthik
Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redlines_Redwood_Legal.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 34 KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 16:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on order form invoicing and taxes

Olivia —

Thanks for the questions and for the PO. Per internal review, here's the proposed commercial language we can agree to and next steps: 

1) Consolidated invoice: We can provide a single annual invoice at Customer's election if the PO reflects the full committed amount. Redwood will still provide monthly line-item detail for reporting. There is a one-time ops fee of $1,500 for manual billing to cover processing; otherwise billing remains monthly. Payment term remains Net 30.

2) Tax exemption: Please upload the TaxCert_Acme.pdf to the DocuSign envelope or the shared Drive link. We'll apply exemptions prospectively; for retrospective requests, please submit within 60 days of the original invoice and we will assess for credit. Approved credits are applied to the next invoice.

3) Credit notes: Dispute window = 45 days from invoice date. Finance will review within 30 days. Credits will be applied to the next invoice; cash refunds are rare and require Finance + Legal signoff.

4) Billing details: Please confirm AP contact and wire instructions in the attached Billing & Payment Details appendix so we can lock routing. 

If Acme is comfortable, I'll attach the redline and update the order form language per Karthik's notes and route a DocuSign envelope for signature. Happy to take a 20-minute call to run through.

Next action for Acme: either confirm consolidated invoice election on the PO OR accept monthly billing. Also upload the tax certificate if you want exemption applied as soon as possible.

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redlines_Redwood_Legal.docx; Billing_Details_Template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 8 KB); TaxCert_Acme.pdf (application/pdf, 48 KB)
